source_title: ‘Beyond the Gates’ Star Mike Manning Shares ‘Tough’ Part of His Move from L.A. to Atlanta (Exclusive) - People.com
source_excerpt:
The actor plays Bradley “Smitty” Smith, a truth-seeking political reporter, on the daytime drama
Mike Manning says he has had a “wild ride” moving from Los Angeles to Atlanta
Speaking with PEOPLE ahead of the 53rd annual Daytime Emmy Awards, the Beyond the Gates actor opens up about the many transitions he had to undergo when he accepted the role of Bradley “Smitty” Smith
Manning says it’s “truly a dream come true” to work on the CBS soap
Mike Manning has had a “wild ride” moving from Los Angeles to Atlanta.
Speaking with PEOPLE ahead of the 53rd annual Daytime Emmy Awards, the Beyond the Gates star opens up about the many transitions he had to undergo when he accepted the role of Bradley “Smitty” Smith. Manning, who was originally living in L.A. with his husband and their two dogs, admits the move has been “a little bit challenging” because of one major reason.
“I’m doing the long-distance thing with my husband right now,” Manning, 39, says. “That’s a little bit challenging, and the dogs are back in L.A. I have two older dogs and they wouldn’t do well in the condo where I’m living right now. So, unfortunately, they are back in Los Angeles with my husband, and that distance has been tough.”
“Luckily, Beyond the Gates gives us ... dark weeks, and I can plan trips to go back to Los Angeles,” he continues. “So I go back as much as I can. But I think in the next year or two we’re going to try to have him move over here to Atlanta, so we’ll see what happens.”
Aside from navigating a long-distance relationship, Manning says he’s certainly “falling in love” with southern living. “The people are so nice,” Manning says, adding, “[and] the food is really good. Within half a mile of my condo in Midtown, I have a dozen restaurants that are now my favorite restaurants. I’ve definitely put on some weight since I’ve lived here because I can’t stop eating.”
The Days of Our Lives alum is enamored by the magnitude of kindness he experiences from the local residents he comes across. Manning explains his time in the South has shown him the true definition and depth of southern hospitality.
“People say it, and I’ve never really lived in the South, so I’ve never experienced it, but people are so kind here,” Manning says, describing Beyond the Gates as the “kindest set” he’s ever worked on. “It’s like aggressive kindness is the norm, and I love that.”
In addition to his move, Manning had to get reacquainted to the fast-paced nature of the soap opera world. The actor, who got his start on the reality TV show The Real World: DC and later starred as Charlie Dale on Days of Our Lives, describes the entire experience as a “wild ride.”
Though Manning enjoyed portraying the villain of the show for two years, he admits he enjoys playing his Beyond the Gates role even more. Starring as a truth-seeking political reporter, Manning explains there’s something special about the fictional town of Fairmont Crest and deep-rooted importance of the show.
“It was fun playing the villain, but I think I enjoy playing Smitty so much because [of] Fairmont Crest and Beyond the Gates ,” he says. “I mean [it’s] the first brand-new soap opera in 25 years and the first-ever hour-long soap to center around a Black family right from its inception, showing Black excellence in a way that we haven’t really seen on soaps before.”
He adds, “Now to have the show nominated for 15 Daytime Emmys — the most any show has ever been nominated in the history of the Daytime Emmys in its first year — is just so reaffirming.”
The soap opera star praises creator and showrunner Michele Val Jean, executive producer Sheila Ducksworth and producer Julie Carruthers for creating the show with intentionality and care.
“These powerful women came forward and said, ‘Look, this show is going to mean something to a lot of people. There has been a community of soap opera fans that have been underserved for the past 76 years. We need a show like this,’” Manning says. “Now for the show to be received by the fans like it is, to be as successful as it is already with the ratings and everything, it’s just truly a dream come true.”

The actor, who’s character is currently being investigated as a prime suspect in a murder case, says he loves seeing his character in “trouble with the Impaler” on the show, adding that he’s excited to see where that storyline takes him.
Despite all the trouble he’s in, Manning doesn’t foresee his character giving his reporting up. He says he’s curious about “what other stories Smitty’s going to try to pursue with his Clark Kent glasses.”
Manning says he’s curious to see what shenanigans his on-screen children Samantha (Najah Jackson) and Tyrell (Jaden Lucas Miller) will get into, as well as what drama the holiday episodes will bring. He’s also excited to dive deeper into his character’s past to learn more about how he became who he is today.
“I would like to see the show dive a little bit more into Smitty’s past and where he comes from,” he says. “We know where [ Brandon Claybon’s Martin Richardson ] comes from. We know how he grew up and what it’s like growing up as a Dupree in a country club. We don’t really know how Smitty grew up, and we’re getting little glimpses of that right now. I would like to see more of that.”
CBS’s Beyond the Gates is streaming on Paramount+.
